Back in the ‘80s, long before I pivoted careers to circus trapeze manufacturing, I was a talent agent for video game characters.  I wasn’t the top dog at my agency, that dude repped Mario, Zelda, Bowser, A-list cats like that.  For me, it was straight second tier. I had Big Boo, Mike from Star Tropics, and LUIGI.  And this last dude, let me tell you, was a PIECE OF WORK.  Couldn’t take him anywhere.  First off, he shows up to the Christmas party two bottles deep, wearing nothing but a g string and a Santa hat, singing the theme to Ducktales.  Gets on the dance floor and starts doing “the worm” on top of a photo of Cory Feldman.  Next thing I know my man is on the roof screaming and crying about his famous big brother, threatening to jump, before LAPD and the fire brigade come out and talk him down. Meanwhile, Mario wasn’t even there because he was receiving another Nintendo Power Man of the Year Award.  But that was nothing. 1990, Nintendo is booming and decides to expand the universe with spinoff games for 20 different characters. Donkey Kong, Yoshi, Toad, even Dr. Wily gets a game. But Luigi?  Nothin doin.  And do you know what the homeboy does when he finds out?  9 day bender in Tijuana. Wound up in a Mexican prison. When we finally got him back he had three tattoos of Jaleel White on his face, and had to have reconstructive surgery on his nose from all the badabing he’d hoovered up the schnozola.  After that I said “life’s too short,” and went back to culinary school.

I understand the challenge of handicapping oneself for early-week puzzles, but always resist the urge to solve only acrosses or downs mainly because I feel it does a disservice to the creators, who put most of their energy and originality into the clues. I'm not virtue signalling here, just don't want to lose out on the potential pleasures of half the clues, and if it also accords respect to the creators then so much the better.

@john ezra 

Well, to each their own. If it makes you feel better I usually do look at the down clues when I finish, or at least the interesting ones. Second, honestly, I think it makes me appreciate the puzzle more. If I do it normally I’ll whiz through it in 7-8 minutes, and probably miss half the clues in one direction or another anyway. This way I spend maybe 15-20 minutes on it; I still have to deduce the down entries, even if I don’t see the clues right away; and most importantly it forces me to really guess, appreciate and use the theme for the solve (assuming the theme is across, which it is usually). Otherwise I might fill out all the theme entries using downs and never have to think much about it. So I don’t think I’m being disrespectful, and I’m certainly not trying to be.
